key_insight: MOSS enables autonomous agents to evolve by rewriting their actual source harness (routing, hooks, dispatch, invariants) rather than only text-mutable artifacts, allowing agents to fix structural failures post-deployment autonomously and safely.
problem_solved: Deployed agentic systems remain largely static and rely on human updates; prior self-evolution methods only modify prompts/skills, leaving code-level logic and routing bugs unaddressed—MOSS fills this gap by enabling safe source-level self-modification.
method: Automated source-level rewriting: synthesize and apply targeted code patches to the agent harness (routing, hook ordering, state invariants) rather than only text artifacts.
Safety-first validation: run unit/behavioral regression tests and sandboxed executions with provenance, versioning, and rollback before promoting patches to production.
Closed-loop monitoring and selection: detect recurrent failures at runtime, propose candidate rewrites, validate them automatically, and iterate with human-in-the-loop oversight as needed.
impact: This approach lets ML/AI teams ship agents that self-correct structural bugs and adapt without frequent human intervention, improving uptime and reducing maintenance cycles while enforcing safety and traceability.

paper_title: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting in Autonomous Agent Systems
